asi.what_worked: End-to-end loop closes cleanly. Pi-smoke green: pi -p against kiln-served qwen3.5-4b on A100. 24 eval tasks completed; only 1 (task_0019) scored 0 — the model wrote an incorrect solution.py for `circular_shift`. The kiln/pi/rubric pipeline produces deterministic SCORE values on stdout for the oracle.
asi.what_failed: Rubric saturation. Baseline composite = 0.958 falls inside the §0 'rubric too lax' band (>=0.95) per the skill. Inspected 5 transcripts by hand; the model is actually solving the easy tasks competently — the problem is that `outcome` (the only sub-score) doesn't penalize wasteful agentic behavior. task_0011 ran 16 bash calls + 2 writes including 7 redundant `python -m doctest` invocations, eventually timed out at 120s — but solution.py was correct at the end, so outcome=1.0 anyway. Saturation here is a rubric design problem, not a capability problem.
asi.next_focus: Multi-component v1 rubric (outcome × (0.30·tool_call_efficiency + 0.20·tested_before_done + 0.10·format_compliance + 0.40)). Outcome stays as hard floor; the agentic sub-scores carry headroom. tool_call_efficiency is the target — its stdev across the 24 baseline rollouts is 0.358, providing strong within-group variance for GRPO. Re-baseline with v1 before iter 1. Bug fix landed in v1: _tested_before_done was reading tc.input but pi uses tc.arguments (OpenAI-style).

asi.what_worked: v1 multi-component rubric lands the cap in the healthy headroom band (composite 0.30 < 0.885 < 0.95). The target sub-score tool_call_efficiency has stdev 0.358 across tasks — strong within-group GRPO signal. The 14 efficient rollouts hit 1.00 composite; the 4 wasteful ones (>10 tool calls including 2 that timed out at 26-27 calls) land in 0.50-0.70. The single outcome=0 (task_0019, circular_shift) demonstrates the rubric correctly zeros composite when the verifier fails.
asi.what_failed: Two saturated sub-scores reduce signal-per-iter: tested_before_done (0.979) and format_compliance (1.000). Could be removed at iter 2+ if they stay saturated through training; for now they're cheap hard-floor guards. outcome itself is at 0.958 — close to the §0 'too lax' threshold but pulled down by task_0019. If iter 1 raises outcome to 1.0 (eliminating the one failure) outcome itself enters the saturation zone and we'd need either harder eval tasks or hidden tests.
